text_blocks.snippet: A consequence of institutional sexism on child support payments is that more than 50% of custodial parents do not receive full child support payments. This is because the system often favors fathers and assumes they are the primary breadwinners, leading to lower child support awards or difficulties in enforcing them.
snippet_highlighted_words: more than 50% of custodial parents do not receive full child support payments

text_blocks.snippet: Explanation: Institutional sexism refers to ingrained biases within systems that disadvantage women. In the child support system, this can manifest as:

list.title: Unequal assumptions about income:
list.snippet: Courts may often presume that fathers have higher incomes and should bear the majority of the financial burden, even if this is not the reality.

list.title: Difficulties in enforcing payments:
list.snippet: Women may face more challenges in getting fathers to comply with court orders, leading to incomplete or nonexistent child support payments.

list.title: Discriminatory practices within the court system:
list.snippet: The procedures and processes involved in determining child support amounts can be biased against women, favoring fathers.
